#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Gitignore pattern tester and reviewer (Python 3 standard library only).

Explains every rule in a .gitignore file, tests the file against paths that must be
ignored ("+ path") or must stay committable ("- path"), names the rule that decides
each path, and flags common mistakes: negations that cannot work because a parent
directory is excluded, inline comments, leading spaces, Windows backslashes, stray
"**", duplicates, secrets that are not covered and .env.example being ignored.

Matching follows git's documented gitignore rules for a single .gitignore at the
repository root: last matching rule wins, "!" re-includes, a trailing "/" matches
directories only, a "/" at the start or in the middle anchors the pattern to the
.gitignore's directory, "*" "?" "[...]" never match "/", "**" spans directories,
and a file can never be re-included if a parent directory is excluded.

Usage:
  python3 gitignore_check.py .gitignore [--test paths.txt] [--json]
  python3 gitignore_check.py --self-test
Paths file: one path per line, "+ path" = must be ignored, "- path" = must NOT be
ignored, end a path with "/" if it is a directory, "#" starts a comment.
Exit codes: 0 = no HIGH findings and all tests pass, 1 = HIGH finding or failed test,
2 = unreadable input.
"""
import argparse, json, re, sys

SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2, "INFO": 3}
SECRET_PROBES = [".env", "config/.env.production", "certs/server.key", "deploy/id_rsa",
                 "secrets/service-account.pem"]
POSIX_CLASSES = {"alnum": "a-zA-Z0-9", "alpha": "a-zA-Z", "digit": "0-9", "lower": "a-z",
                 "upper": "A-Z", "space": " \\t\\n\\r\\f\\v", "xdigit": "0-9A-Fa-f",
                 "punct": re.escape("!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~"), "blank": " \\t"}


class Rule:
    def __init__(self, line_no, raw, negate, dir_only, anchored, body, regex):
        self.line_no, self.raw, self.negate, self.dir_only = line_no, raw, negate, dir_only
        self.anchored, self.body, self.regex = anchored, body, regex

    def matches(self, rel_path, is_dir):
        if self.dir_only and not is_dir:
            return False
        target = rel_path if self.anchored else rel_path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        return self.regex.fullmatch(target) is not None

    def label(self):
        return f"L{self.line_no} `{self.raw}`"


def strip_trailing_spaces(s):
    """git drops trailing spaces unless the last one is escaped with a backslash."""
    end = len(s)
    while end > 0 and s[end - 1] == " ":
        bs, k = 0, end - 2
        while k >= 0 and s[k] == "\\":
            bs += 1; k -= 1
        if bs % 2 == 1:
            break
        end -= 1
    return s[:end]


def class_to_regex(body):
    out, m = "", 0
    while m < len(body):
        ch = body[m]
        if ch == "[" and body.startswith("[:", m):
            end = body.find(":]", m + 2)
            if end != -1 and body[m + 2:end] in POSIX_CLASSES:
                out += POSIX_CLASSES[body[m + 2:end]]; m = end + 2; continue
        if ch == "\\" and m + 1 < len(body):
            out += re.escape(body[m + 1]); m += 2; continue
        if ch == "-" and 0 < m < len(body) - 1:
            out += "-"; m += 1; continue
        out += re.escape(ch); m += 1
    return out


def glob_to_regex(p):
    out, i, n = "", 0, len(p)
    while i < n:
        c = p[i]
        if c == "\\":
            if i + 1 < n:
                out += re.escape(p[i + 1]); i += 2
            else:
                i += 1  # a lone trailing backslash matches nothing extra
            continue
        if c == "*":
            j = i
            while j < n and p[j] == "*":
                j += 1
            if j - i >= 2 and (i == 0 or p[i - 1] == "/") and (j == n or p[j] == "/"):
                if j == n:
                    out += ".*"; i = j
                else:
                    out += "(?:.*/)?"; i = j + 1
                continue
            out += "[^/]*"; i = j; continue
        if c == "?":
            out += "[^/]"; i += 1; continue
        if c == "[":
            j = i + 1
            neg = j < n and p[j] in "!^"
            if neg:
                j += 1
            k = j + 1 if j < n and p[j] == "]" else j
            while k < n and p[k] != "]":
                if p[k] == "[" and p.startswith("[:", k):
                    end = p.find(":]", k + 2)
                    if end != -1:
                        k = end + 2; continue
                k += 2 if p[k] == "\\" else 1
            if k >= n:
                out += re.escape("["); i += 1; continue
            cls = class_to_regex(p[j:k])
            out += ("[^/" + cls + "]") if neg else ("(?!/)[" + cls + "]")
            i = k + 1; continue
        out += re.escape(c); i += 1
    return out


def parse_rules(text):
    rules, findings, seen = [], [], {}
    for no, raw in enumerate(text.split("\n"), 1):
        if raw.endswith("\r"):
            findings.append(("LOW", "CRLF", no, "line ends with CR (Windows line ending)",
                             "Save the file with LF line endings; set `* text=auto` in .gitattributes."))
            raw = raw[:-1]
        if not raw.strip() or raw.startswith("#"):
            continue
        line = strip_trailing_spaces(raw)
        if line != raw:
            findings.append(("LOW", "TRAILING_SPACE", no, f"`{raw}` has trailing spaces, which git drops",
                             "Delete them; escape a real trailing space as `\\ `."))
        if raw[0] in " \t":
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "LEADING_SPACE", no, f"`{raw}` starts with whitespace, which git keeps as part of the name, so it matches nothing useful",
                             "Remove the leading whitespace."))
        m = re.search(r"\s#", line)
        if m:
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "INLINE_COMMENT", no, f"`{line}`: git has no inline comments, so `{line[m.start():].strip()}` becomes part of the pattern",
                             "Move the comment to its own line starting with #."))
        if re.search(r"\\[A-Za-z0-9_]", line):
            findings.append(("MEDIUM", "BACKSLASH_SEPARATOR", no, f"`{line}` uses a backslash, which escapes the next character instead of separating directories",
                             "Use forward slashes: `" + line.replace("\\", "/") + "`."))
        key = line.strip()
        if key in seen:
            findings.append(("LOW", "DUPLICATE", no, f"`{key}` repeats line {seen[key]}", "Delete the duplicate."))
        else:
            seen[key] = no
        negate = line.startswith("!")
        body = line[1:] if negate else line
        if body.startswith("\\!") or body.startswith("\\#"):
            body = body[1:]
        if negate and not body:
            findings.append(("LOW", "EMPTY_NEGATION", no, "`!` alone does nothing", "Delete the line."))
            continue
        dir_only = body.endswith("/") and not body.endswith("\\/")
        if dir_only:
            body = body.rstrip("/")
        if not body:
            continue
        anchored = "/" in body
        if body.startswith("/"):
            body = body[1:]
        if any((m.start() > 0 and body[m.start() - 1] != "/") or (m.end() < len(body) and body[m.end()] != "/")
               for m in re.finditer(r"\*{2,}", body)):
            findings.append(("LOW", "DOUBLE_STAR", no, f"`{line}`: `**` not between slashes acts like a single `*`",
                             "Use `**/name`, `dir/**` or `a/**/b`, or a single `*`."))
        rules.append(Rule(no, line, negate, dir_only, anchored, body, re.compile(glob_to_regex(body), re.S)))
    return rules, findings


def last_match(rules, rel_path, is_dir):
    hit = None
    for r in rules:
        if r.matches(rel_path, is_dir):
            hit = r
    return hit


def check_path(rules, path):
    """Return (ignored, reason, blocked_rule) following git's parent-directory rule."""
    is_dir = path.endswith("/")
    parts = [p for p in path.strip("/").split("/") if p]
    for k in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
        sub = "/".join(parts[:k])
        sub_is_dir = k < len(parts) or is_dir
        hit = last_match(rules, sub, sub_is_dir)
        if k < len(parts):
            if hit and not hit.negate:
                own = last_match(rules, "/".join(parts), is_dir)
                blocked = own if own and own.negate else None
                return True, f"parent `{sub}/` excluded by {hit.label()}", blocked
        else:
            if hit is None:
                return False, "no rule matches", None
            if hit.negate:
                return False, f"re-included by {hit.label()}", None
            return True, f"ignored by {hit.label()}", None
    return False, "empty path", None


def literal_dirs(body):
    parts = body.split("/")[:-1]
    out = []
    for p in parts:
        if any(ch in p for ch in "*?[\\"):
            break
        out.append(p)
    return out


def lint_negations(rules):
    findings = []
    for idx, r in enumerate(rules):
        if not r.negate or not r.anchored:
            continue
        before = rules[:idx]
        dirs = literal_dirs(r.body)
        for k in range(1, len(dirs) + 1):
            sub = "/".join(dirs[:k])
            hit = last_match(before, sub, True)
            if hit and not hit.negate:
                findings.append(("HIGH", "NEGATION_BLOCKED", r.line_no,
                                 f"`{r.raw.strip()}` can never apply: its parent directory `{sub}/` is excluded by {hit.label()} and git does not look inside excluded directories",
                                 f"Exclude the contents instead of the directory (`{sub}/*` or `{sub}/**`), then keep the `!` rule; or re-include `!{sub}/` first."))
                break
    return findings


def lint_secrets(rules):
    findings = []
    missing = [p for p in SECRET_PROBES if not check_path(rules, p)[0]]
    if missing:
        findings.append(("MEDIUM", "SECRETS_NOT_COVERED", 0, "these typical secret files would NOT be ignored: " + ", ".join(missing),
                         "Add `.env`, `.env.*` (with `!.env.example`), `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*` if the project could ever contain them."))
    if check_path(rules, ".env.example")[0]:
        findings.append(("LOW", "ENV_EXAMPLE_IGNORED", 0, "`.env.example` is ignored, so the documented template cannot be committed",
                         "Add `!.env.example` after the .env rule."))
    return findings


def explain(rule):
    body = rule.body
    kind = "directories" if rule.dir_only else "files or directories"
    verb = "Re-includes" if rule.negate else "Ignores"
    wild = any(ch in body for ch in "*?[")
    if rule.anchored and body.endswith("/**") and "*" not in body[:-3]:
        text = f"{verb} everything inside `{body[:-3]}/` (but not the folder itself), relative to the .gitignore folder"
    elif rule.anchored and body.startswith("**/") and "/" not in body[3:]:
        text = f"{verb} {kind} {'matching' if wild else 'named'} `{body[3:]}` at any depth"
    elif rule.anchored:
        text = f"{verb} {kind} {'matching' if wild else 'at'} `{body}` relative to the .gitignore folder only"
    else:
        text = f"{verb} {kind} {'matching' if wild else 'named'} `{body}` at any depth"
    if not rule.negate and not body.endswith("/**"):
        text += "; a matched directory hides everything inside it"
    if rule.negate:
        text += " (only works if no parent directory is excluded)"
    return text + "."


def read_tests(text):
    tests = []
    for no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        s = line.strip()
        if not s or s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if s[0] not in "+-" or len(s) < 3:
            raise ValueError(f"paths file line {no}: expected '+ path' or '- path', got {line!r}")
        tests.append((s[0] == "+", s[1:].strip()))
    return tests


def review(gi_text, tests_text=None):
    rules, findings = parse_rules(gi_text)
    findings += lint_negations(rules)
    findings += lint_secrets(rules)
    anchored = [r.line_no for r in rules if r.anchored and not r.negate and "/" in r.body
                and not r.raw.startswith(("/", "**/")) and not r.body.endswith("/**")]
    if anchored:
        findings.append(("INFO", "ANCHORED_BY_SLASH", anchored[0],
                         "lines " + ", ".join(map(str, anchored)) + " contain a slash, so they only match relative to the .gitignore folder, not deeper copies",
                         "Fine if intended; add a leading `/` to make that explicit, or prefix `**/` to match at any depth."))
    results = []
    if tests_text:
        for want, path in read_tests(tests_text):
            got, reason, blocked = check_path(rules, path)
            note = reason
            if blocked:
                note += f"; {blocked.label()} cannot re-include it"
            results.append({"path": path, "expect": "ignored" if want else "kept",
                            "actual": "ignored" if got else "kept", "pass": got == want, "why": note})
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (SEV_ORDER[f[0]], f[2]))
    return {"rules": [{"line": r.line_no, "pattern": r.raw, "meaning": explain(r)} for r in rules],
            "findings": [dict(zip(("severity", "code", "line", "problem", "fix"), f)) for f in findings],
            "tests": results}


def render(name, rep):
    out = [f"# .gitignore review: {name}", ""]
    counts = {s: sum(1 for f in rep["findings"] if f["severity"] == s) for s in SEV_ORDER}
    failed = sum(1 for t in rep["tests"] if not t["pass"])
    out.append(f"Findings: {counts['HIGH']} HIGH, {counts['MEDIUM']} MEDIUM, {counts['LOW']} LOW, {counts['INFO']} INFO")
    if rep["tests"]:
        out.append(f"Tests: {len(rep['tests']) - failed}/{len(rep['tests'])} passed")
    out += ["", "## Rules", "", "| Line | Pattern | Meaning |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rep["rules"]:
        out.append(f"| {r['line']} | `{r['pattern']}` | {r['meaning']} |")
    if rep["tests"]:
        out += ["", "## Path tests", "", "| Result | Path | Expected | Actual | Decided by |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for t in rep["tests"]:
            out.append(f"| {'PASS' if t['pass'] else 'FAIL'} | `{t['path']}` | {t['expect']} | {t['actual']} | {t['why']} |")
    out += ["", "## Findings", ""]
    if rep["findings"]:
        out += ["| Severity | Code | Line | Problem | Fix |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for f in rep["findings"]:
            out.append(f"| {f['severity']} | {f['code']} | {f['line'] or '-'} | {f['problem']} | {f['fix']} |")
    else:
        out.append("No findings.")
    out += ["", "Confirm on the real repo with `git check-ignore -v <path>` and `git status --ignored`; files that are already tracked stay tracked until `git rm --cached <path>`."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    cases = []
    def t(name, cond):
        cases.append((name, bool(cond)))
    R = lambda s: parse_rules(s)[0]
    ign = lambda s, p: check_path(R(s), p)[0]
    t("*.log matches at any depth", ign("*.log", "a/b/c.log") and ign("*.log", "x.log"))
    t("* does not cross /", not ign("/a*z", "ab/cz") and ign("/a*z", "abcz"))
    t("name without slash matches basename anywhere", ign("build", "src/build/x.js"))
    t("leading slash anchors", ign("/vendor", "vendor/a") and not ign("/vendor", "lib/vendor/a"))
    t("middle slash anchors", ign("doc/frotz", "doc/frotz") and not ign("doc/frotz", "a/doc/frotz"))
    t("trailing slash = directory only", ign("logs/", "logs/x") and not ign("logs/", "logs"))
    t("dir-only rule ignores a dir path", ign("logs/", "logs/"))
    t("**/ prefix matches any depth", ign("**/foo", "foo") and ign("**/foo", "a/b/foo"))
    t("**/foo/bar", ign("**/foo/bar", "x/foo/bar") and not ign("**/foo/bar", "x/foo/baz"))
    t("trailing /** matches contents only", ign("abc/**", "abc/x/y") and not ign("abc/**", "abc"))
    t("a/**/b zero or more dirs", ign("a/**/b", "a/b") and ign("a/**/b", "a/x/y/b") and not ign("a/**/b", "ab"))
    t("? matches one char not /", ign("/a?c", "abc") and not ign("/a?c", "a/c"))
    t("[abc] class", ign("file[12].txt", "file1.txt") and not ign("file[12].txt", "file3.txt"))
    t("[!x] negated class", ign("f[!0-9]", "fa") and not ign("f[!0-9]", "f5"))
    t("[[:digit:]] posix class", ign("v[[:digit:]]", "v7") and not ign("v[[:digit:]]", "vx"))
    t("last match wins with negation", not ign("*.txt\n!keep.txt", "keep.txt") and ign("*.txt\n!keep.txt", "a.txt"))
    t("order matters", ign("!keep.txt\n*.txt", "keep.txt"))
    t("parent dir excluded blocks negation", ign("logs/\n!logs/.gitkeep", "logs/.gitkeep"))
    t("dir/* allows negation", not ign("logs/*\n!logs/.gitkeep", "logs/.gitkeep"))
    t("dir/** allows negation", not ign("coverage/**\n!coverage/README.md", "coverage/README.md"))
    t("re-include dir then file", not ign("/a/*\n!/a/b/\n/a/b/*\n!/a/b/c", "a/b/c"))
    t("escaped # and !", ign("\\#notes", "#notes") and ign("\\!bang", "!bang"))
    t("comment lines skipped", not ign("# *.log", "a.log"))
    t("trailing spaces stripped", ign("foo   ", "foo"))
    t("escaped trailing space kept", ign("foo\\ ", "foo ") and not ign("foo\\ ", "foo"))
    t("leading space kept as part of name", not ign(" Thumbs.db", "Thumbs.db"))
    t("inline comment becomes pattern", not ign("secrets.yml # x", "secrets.yml"))
    t("backslash escapes, not a separator", not ign("src\\gen", "src/gen/a.ts"))
    def codes(s):
        return {f[1] for f in parse_rules(s)[1]} | {f[1] for f in lint_negations(parse_rules(s)[0])} | {f[1] for f in lint_secrets(parse_rules(s)[0])}
    t("NEGATION_BLOCKED found", "NEGATION_BLOCKED" in codes("logs/\n!logs/.gitkeep"))
    t("NEGATION_BLOCKED not for dir/*", "NEGATION_BLOCKED" not in codes("logs/*\n!logs/.gitkeep"))
    t("NEGATION_BLOCKED via dir/* deeper", "NEGATION_BLOCKED" in codes("a/*\n!a/b/c.txt"))
    t("INLINE_COMMENT found", "INLINE_COMMENT" in codes("x.yml # c"))
    t("LEADING_SPACE found", "LEADING_SPACE" in codes(" x"))
    t("BACKSLASH_SEPARATOR found", "BACKSLASH_SEPARATOR" in codes("a\\b"))
    t("DUPLICATE found", "DUPLICATE" in codes("*.log\n*.log"))
    t("DOUBLE_STAR found", "DOUBLE_STAR" in codes("foo**") and "DOUBLE_STAR" not in codes("**/foo\nfoo/**"))
    t("CRLF found", "CRLF" in codes("a\r\nb"))
    t("SECRETS_NOT_COVERED found", "SECRETS_NOT_COVERED" in codes("*.log"))
    t("secrets covered", "SECRETS_NOT_COVERED" not in codes(".env\n.env.*\n!.env.example\n*.key\n*.pem\nid_rsa*"))
    t("ENV_EXAMPLE_IGNORED found", "ENV_EXAMPLE_IGNORED" in codes(".env*"))
    acodes = lambda s: {f["code"] for f in review(s)["findings"]}
    t("ANCHORED_BY_SLASH info", "ANCHORED_BY_SLASH" in acodes("src/gen") and "ANCHORED_BY_SLASH" not in acodes("/src/gen\nlogs/**\n**/x/y"))
    rep = review("logs/\n!logs/.gitkeep\n", "+ logs/a.log\n- logs/.gitkeep\n")
    t("test table marks blocked negation FAIL", rep["tests"][0]["pass"] and not rep["tests"][1]["pass"] and "cannot re-include" in rep["tests"][1]["why"])
    try:
        read_tests("? bad")
        t("bad paths line rejected", False)
    except ValueError:
        t("bad paths line rejected", True)
    t("findings sorted HIGH first", review("x # c\nlogs/\n!logs/a\n")["findings"][0]["severity"] == "HIGH")
    passed = sum(ok for _, ok in cases)
    for name, ok in cases:
        print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + name)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(cases)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(cases) else 1


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("gitignore", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--test", help="paths file with '+ path' (must be ignored) and '- path' (must be kept)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.gitignore:
        ap.print_usage(sys.stderr); return 2
    try:
        gi = open(a.gitignore, encoding="utf-8", newline="").read()
        tests = open(a.test, encoding="utf-8").read() if a.test else None
        rep = review(gi, tests)
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr); return 2
    print(json.dumps(rep, indent=2) if a.json else render(a.gitignore, rep))
    bad = any(f["severity"] == "HIGH" for f in rep["findings"]) or any(not t["pass"] for t in rep["tests"])
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Scaling caveats

## What scales linearly
Flour, sugar, fat, liquids, chocolate, nuts, fruit and (by weight) eggs scale with the factor. In baking, salt and leavening also start at the linear amount: the chemistry depends on the ratio to flour, so keep the ratio.

## Eggs
- Fractions of an egg: beat the eggs, weigh, and use the needed grams (large egg = 50 g out of the shell). 3.66 eggs = 3 eggs + 33 g beaten egg (about 2 tbsp).
- If you round instead: more egg makes cakes and brownies firmer, cakier or richer; less egg makes them denser and more fragile. Round up for cakes, down for fudgy brownies and cookies when in doubt.
- Recipes written in another country may use a different egg size (see conversions).

## Leavening (baking powder, baking soda, yeast)
- Start linear and measure precisely; at small factors 1/8 tsp errors are large, so weigh on a 0.1 g scale.
- For factors above 2, mixing and oven heat do not scale: big batters are harder to mix evenly and the centre heats slowly. Make separate batches of the original size when you can.
- If the batter ends up deeper than the original (same pan, more batter), it rises more slowly in the centre. Do not "fix" this with more leavening; use a wider pan or lower the oven and bake longer.
- Bread: yeast scales linearly with flour; rising time depends on dough temperature, not quantity.

## Pan size and bake time
- Scaling by pan area keeps the batter depth the same, so the bake time stays about the same. Start checking 5 minutes early.
- Same recipe in a different pan: depth ratio = old area / new area. Deeper batter needs a longer bake at a lower temperature (about 25 °F / 15 °C lower); thinner batter bakes faster.
- Fill cake pans at most 2/3 full, brownie pans about halfway.
- Glass and dark metal pans bake faster at the edges: lower 25 °F / 15 °C.
- Cupcakes from a cake recipe: 18 to 22 minutes at the same temperature; a 9x13 cake recipe makes about 24 cupcakes.
- Never multiply the bake time by the factor. Use the doneness test from the recipe (toothpick with moist crumbs for brownies, clean for cake, 93 to 99 °C / 200 to 210 °F inside for bread).

## Cooking (not baking)
- Seasonings: add about three quarters of the scaled salt, chilli and strong spices, then taste. A bigger pot evaporates differently.
- Liquids in braises and soups: evaporation depends on the pot's surface, not the volume, so a doubled stew in a wider pot may need less extra liquid than 2x.
- Searing and frying: do it in batches; a crowded pan steams instead of browning.
- Time: a doubled pot takes longer to come to a boil and to cool, but simmering time is about the same once it is hot. Roasts depend on thickness, not weight: use a thermometer.
- Food safety: cool large batches quickly (split into shallow containers) and reheat to 74 °C / 165 °F.

## Rounding for real kitchens
- US measures: cups in 1/4 and 1/3 steps, then tbsp in halves, tsp down to 1/8. Below 1/8 tsp = a pinch.
- Metric: grams to 0.5 g below 10 g, 1 g below 100 g, 5 g below 1 kg.
- Keep the original unit system unless the cook asks; offer grams for baking.
- Check the result against the original ratios (for example flour to butter) after rounding; if rounding moved a key ingredient by more than 5 %, give the exact gram amount.

"""Recipe scaling and unit converter (Python 3 standard library only).

rounds to amounts you can measure, and flags baking caveats: fractional eggs, leavening
at large factors, batter depth changes when the pan does not scale with the recipe,
tiny amounts, seasoning and cooking time.

Input CSV columns: quantity,unit,ingredient,note
  quantity: 2 | 1.5 | 3/4 | 1 1/2 | ½   unit: tsp tbsp cup fl oz pint quart ml l g kg oz lb stick
  each (or empty) for counted items such as eggs.
Usage:
  python3 scale_recipe.py recipe.csv --servings 4 10 [--to us|metric|weight|keep]
  python3 scale_recipe.py recipe.csv --from-pan 8x8 --to-pan 9x13 --baking --oven 350F --time 20-25
  python3 scale_recipe.py recipe.csv --factor 0.5 --to weight --json
  python3 scale_recipe.py --self-test

                "quarts": "quart", "qt": "quart", "milliliter": "ml", "milliliters": "ml", "mL": "ml",
                "liter": "l", "liters": "l", "litre": "l", "litres": "l", "L": "l", "gram": "g", "grams": "g",
                "kilogram": "kg", "kilograms": "kg", "ounce": "oz", "ounces": "oz", "pound": "lb", "pounds": "lb",
                "lbs": "lb", "sticks": "stick", "": "each", "x": "each", "whole": "each", "pc": "each",
                "pcs": "each", "piece": "each", "pieces": "each", "clove": "each", "cloves": "each",
                "large": "each", "medium": "each", "small": "each", "pinch": "pinch", "pinches": "pinch",
                "dash": "pinch"}
# grams per US cup (spoon-and-level). Longest matching name wins.
DENSITY = {
    "all-purpose flour": 125, "plain flour": 125, "flour": 125, "bread flour": 127, "cake flour": 114,
    "whole wheat flour": 113, "almond flour": 96, "cornstarch": 112, "cornflour": 112,
    "granulated sugar": 200, "caster sugar": 200, "sugar": 200, "brown sugar": 213,
    "powdered sugar": 120, "icing sugar": 120, "confectioners sugar": 120,
    "butter": 227, "water": 237, "milk": 242, "buttermilk": 242, "heavy cream": 238, "cream": 238,
    "sour cream": 242, "yogurt": 245, "vegetable oil": 218, "canola oil": 218, "olive oil": 216, "oil": 218,
    "honey": 340, "maple syrup": 322, "golden syrup": 340, "cocoa powder": 85, "cocoa": 85,
    "rolled oats": 90, "oats": 90, "chocolate chips": 170, "rice": 185, "chopped nuts": 120,
    "walnuts": 120, "pecans": 110, "raisins": 150, "peanut butter": 270,
    "table salt": 288, "fine salt": 288, "salt": 288, "kosher salt": None,
    "baking soda": 230, "bicarbonate of soda": 230, "baking powder": 192, "instant yeast": 149,
    "active dry yeast": 149, "yeast": 149, "vanilla extract": 202, "vanilla": 202,
    "ground cinnamon": 125, "cinnamon": 125,
}
LEAVENERS = ("baking soda", "bicarbonate", "baking powder", "yeast", "cream of tartar")
SEASONINGS = ("salt", "pepper", "chili", "chilli", "cayenne", "pepper flakes", "garlic powder", "curry", "cumin", "paprika")
EGG_G = {"egg": 50.0, "yolk": 18.0, "white": 32.0}  # US large egg out of shell
UNICODE_FRAC = {"½": .5, "¼": .25, "¾": .75, "⅓": 1 / 3, "⅔": 2 / 3, "⅛": .125, "⅜": .375, "⅝": .625, "⅞": .875}
SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2, "INFO": 3}


def parse_qty(s):
    s = s.strip()
    for ch, v in UNICODE_FRAC.items():
        if ch in s:
            rest = s.replace(ch, "").strip()
            return (float(rest) if rest else 0.0) + v
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)\s+(\d+)/(\d+)", s)
    if m:
        return int(m[1]) + int(m[2]) / int(m[3])
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)/(\d+)", s)
    if m:
        return int(m[1]) / int(m[2])
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+", s)
    if m:
        return float(s)
    raise ValueError(f"cannot read quantity {s!r}")


def norm_unit(u):
    u = u.strip()
    if u in UNIT_ALIASES:
        return UNIT_ALIASES[u]
    low = u.lower().rstrip(".")
    if low in ML or low in G or low in ("each", "pinch"):
        return low
    if low in UNIT_ALIASES:
        return UNIT_ALIASES[low]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown unit {u!r}")


def density_for(name):
    low = name.lower()
    best = None
    for key in DENSITY:
        if re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(key) + r"\b", low) and (best is None or len(key) > len(best)):
            best = key
    return (best, DENSITY[best]) if best else (None, None)


def egg_kind(name):
    low = name.lower()
    if "yolk" in low:
        return "yolk"
    if "white" in low and "egg" in low:
        return "white"
    if re.search(r"\beggs?\b", low):
        return "egg"
    return None


def parse_pan(spec):
    s = spec.strip().lower().replace(" ", "").replace("inch", "").replace("in", "").replace('"', "")
    cm = s.endswith("cm")
    if cm:
        s = s[:-2]
    k = 1 / 2.54 if cm else 1.0
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(?:round)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?:round)?", s)
    if m and "round" in s:
        d = float(m[1]) * k
        return math.pi * (d / 2) ** 2, f"{spec} round ({d:.1f} in)"
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(?:loaf|square|rect)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)x(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", s)
    if m:
        a, b = float(m[1]) * k, float(m[2]) * k
        return a * b, f"{spec} ({a:.1f} x {b:.1f} in)"
    raise ValueError(f"cannot read pan size {spec!r} (use 9x13, 20x30cm, round9, round23cm, loaf9x5)")


def frac_str(x, denoms=(2, 3, 4, 8)):
    whole = int(x)
    rest = x - whole
    best = (abs(rest), 0, 1)
    for d in denoms:
        n = round(rest * d)
        if 0 < n < d and abs(rest - n / d) < best[0] - 1e-9:
            best = (abs(rest - n / d), n, d)
    if abs(rest - 1) < best[0]:
        return str(whole + 1)
    _, n, d = best
    if n == 0:
        return str(whole)
    g = math.gcd(n, d)
    return (f"{whole} " if whole else "") + f"{n // g}/{d // g}"


def frac_val(s):
    return parse_qty(s)


def cup_word(x):
    return "cups" if x > 1 + 1e-9 else "cup"


def fmt_us_volume(ml):
    cups = ml / ML["cup"]
    if cups >= 0.25 - 1e-9:
        s = frac_str(cups, (2, 3, 4))
        err = abs(frac_val(s) - cups) * ML["cup"]
        if err >= ML["tbsp"] * 0.75:
            base = math.floor(cups * 4) / 4
            tb = (cups - base) * ML["cup"] / ML["tbsp"]
            bs = frac_str(base, (4,))
            return (f"{bs} {cup_word(base)} + " if base else "") + f"{frac_str(tb, (2,))} tbsp"
        return f"{s} {cup_word(frac_val(s))}"
    tbsp = ml / ML["tbsp"]
    if tbsp >= 1 - 1e-9:
        return f"{frac_str(tbsp, (2,))} tbsp"
    tsp = ml / ML["tsp"]
    if tsp < 1 / 16:
        return "pinch"
    return f"{frac_str(tsp, (2, 4, 8))} tsp"


def round_metric(x):
    if x < 10:
        return round(x * 2) / 2
    if x < 100:
        return round(x)
    if x < 1000:
        return round(x / 5) * 5
    return round(x / 10) * 10


def fmt_num(x):
    return f"{x:g}"


def fmt_metric(amount, unit):
    v = round_metric(amount)
    if v >= 2000:
        return f"{fmt_num(v / 1000)} {'kg' if unit == 'g' else 'l'}"
    return f"{fmt_num(v)} {unit}"


def fmt_us_weight(g):
    oz = g / G["oz"]
    if oz >= 16:
        lb = oz / 16
        return f"{frac_str(lb, (4,))} lb"
    return f"{frac_str(oz, (2, 4))} oz" if oz >= 1 else f"{fmt_num(round(oz, 2))} oz"


def convert(row, factor, target):
    """Return dict with scaled display and notes for one ingredient row."""
    qty, unit, name = row["qty"] * factor, row["unit"], row["ingredient"]
    key, dens = density_for(name)
    egg = egg_kind(name)
    out = {"ingredient": name, "original": row["original"], "scaled_qty": qty, "unit": unit, "notes": []}
    if unit == "each":
        if egg:
            g = qty * EGG_G[egg]
            out["display"] = f"{fmt_num(round(qty, 2))} ({fmt_metric(g, 'g')} beaten)"
        else:
            out["display"] = fmt_num(round(qty, 2))
        return out
    if unit == "pinch":
        out["display"] = f"{fmt_num(round(qty, 2))} pinch"
        return out
    if unit in ML:
        ml = qty * ML[unit]
        out["ml"] = ml
        if target == "weight":
            if dens:
                out["display"] = fmt_metric(ml / ML["cup"] * dens, "g")
                out["also"] = fmt_us_volume(ml)
            else:
                out["display"] = fmt_metric(ml, "ml")
                out["also"] = fmt_us_volume(ml)
                out["notes"].append("NO_DENSITY")
        elif target == "metric" or (target == "keep" and unit in ("ml", "l")):
            out["display"] = fmt_metric(ml, "ml")
            out["also"] = fmt_us_volume(ml)
        else:
            out["display"] = fmt_us_volume(ml)
            out["also"] = fmt_metric(ml, "ml") if not dens else fmt_metric(ml / ML["cup"] * dens, "g")
        return out
    g = qty * G[unit]
    out["g"] = g
    if target == "us" or (target == "keep" and unit in ("oz", "lb", "stick")):
        if unit == "stick" and target == "keep":
            out["display"] = f"{frac_str(qty, (2, 4))} stick ({fmt_metric(g, 'g')})"
        else:
            out["display"] = fmt_us_weight(g)
        out["also"] = fmt_metric(g, "g")
    else:
        out["display"] = fmt_metric(g, "g")
        if dens:
            out["also"] = fmt_us_volume(g / dens * ML["cup"])
    return out


def read_recipe(text):
    rows = []
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text.lstrip("\ufeff")))
    need = {"quantity", "unit", "ingredient"}
    if not reader.fieldnames or not need <= {f.strip().lower() for f in reader.fieldnames}:
        raise ValueError("CSV header must include quantity,unit,ingredient (note optional)")
    for i, r in enumerate(reader, 2):
        r = {k.strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items() if k}
        if not r.get("ingredient"):
            continue
        try:
            qty = parse_qty(r["quantity"])
            unit = norm_unit(r.get("unit", ""))
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"line {i}: {e}")
        orig = f"{r['quantity']} {r.get('unit', '')}".strip()
        rows.append({"qty": qty, "unit": unit, "ingredient": r["ingredient"], "note": r.get("note", ""), "original": orig})
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("no ingredient rows")
    return rows


def oven(temp):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*°?\s*([CcFf])\s*", temp)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot read oven temperature {temp!r} (use 350F or 180C)")
    v, u = float(m[1]), m[2].upper()
    if u == "F":
        c = (v - 32) * 5 / 9
        return f"{v:g}°F = {round(c / 10) * 10:g}°C (fan oven {round(c / 10) * 10 - 20:g}°C)"
    f = v * 9 / 5 + 32
    return f"{v:g}°C = {round(f / 25) * 25:g}°F"


def scale(rows, factor, target="keep", baking=False, depth_ratio=None, pan_change=None, bake_time=None):
    items = [convert(r, factor, target) for r in rows]
    findings = []
    for it, r in zip(items, rows):
        name = r["ingredient"].lower()
        egg = egg_kind(name)
        if egg and r["unit"] == "each":
            q = it["scaled_qty"]
            whole = math.floor(q + 1e-9)
            if abs(q - round(q)) > 0.15:
                extra = (q - whole) * EGG_G[egg]
                findings.append(("MEDIUM", "EGG_FRACTION", r["ingredient"],
                                 f"scales to {q:.2f} {egg}s",
                                 f"Use {whole} whole {egg}{'s' if whole != 1 else ''} plus {round(extra):g} g beaten {egg} (a large {egg} is about {EGG_G[egg]:g} g out of the shell), or round to {round(q)} and expect a {'richer' if round(q) > q else 'drier'} result."))
        if "NO_DENSITY" in it["notes"]:
            findings.append(("LOW", "NO_DENSITY", r["ingredient"], "no density in the table, so it stays in volume",
                             "Weigh it once, or look up grams per cup; for kosher salt the brand matters (Diamond Crystal about 136 g/cup, Morton about 240 g/cup)."))
        ml = it.get("ml")
        if ml is not None and ml / ML["tsp"] < 1 / 8 and r["unit"] in ML:
            findings.append(("LOW", "TINY_AMOUNT", r["ingredient"], f"scales to {ml / ML['tsp']:.2f} tsp",
                             "Use a pinch or a 1/8 tsp measure; for leavening weigh on a 0.1 g scale."))
        if baking and any(w in name for w in LEAVENERS) and (factor > 2 or factor < 0.5):
            findings.append(("LOW", "LEAVENING", r["ingredient"], f"leavening scaled x{factor:.2f}",
                             "Linear scaling is the starting point; measure exactly (weigh), and for factors above 2 consider separate batches because mixing and oven heat do not scale."))
        if not baking and factor > 2 and any(w in name for w in SEASONINGS):
            findings.append(("INFO", "SEASONING", r["ingredient"], f"seasoning scaled x{factor:.2f}",
                             "Add about three quarters, then taste and adjust; evaporation and pot size change how salty or hot it ends up."))
    if baking and (factor > 3 or factor < 1 / 3):
        findings.append(("MEDIUM", "BIG_FACTOR", "-", f"baking recipe scaled x{factor:.2f}",
                         "Bake in several batches of the original size, or check mixer bowl capacity; never multiply the bake time."))
    if depth_ratio is not None:
        sev = "HIGH" if (depth_ratio > 1.5 or depth_ratio < 0.67) else ("MEDIUM" if (depth_ratio > 1.25 or depth_ratio < 0.8) else None)
        if sev and baking:
            if depth_ratio > 1:
                fix = "Batter will be deeper: lower the oven by 25°F/15°C, bake longer and test the centre, keep the pan at most 2/3 full, or use a bigger pan."
            else:
                fix = "Batter will be thinner: start checking 25 to 40 % earlier, or use a smaller pan."
            findings.append((sev, "DEPTH_CHANGE", "-", f"batter depth changes x{depth_ratio:.2f} versus the original pan", fix))
    if baking and pan_change:
        if depth_ratio is None or 0.9 <= depth_ratio <= 1.1:
            tip = "Batter depth stays about the same, so the bake time stays about the same; start checking 5 minutes early. Glass or dark pans bake faster: lower 25°F/15°C."
        elif 0.8 <= depth_ratio <= 1.25:
            tip = f"Batter depth changes slightly (x{depth_ratio:.2f}); {'bake a few minutes longer' if depth_ratio > 1 else 'start checking a few minutes early'} and test the centre."
        else:
            tip = "See DEPTH_CHANGE for time and temperature."
        if bake_time:
            tip = f"Original {bake_time} min. " + tip
        findings.append(("INFO", "PAN_TIME", "-", pan_change, tip))
    if not baking and factor > 1.5:
        findings.append(("INFO", "COOK_TIME", "-", f"scaled x{factor:.2f}",
                         "Cooking time does not scale with quantity: brown meat in batches, allow longer to come to a boil, and use a pot that keeps the depth similar."))
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: SEV_ORDER[f[0]])
    return items, [dict(zip(("severity", "code", "ingredient", "problem", "fix"), f)) for f in findings]


def render(path, factor, how, target, items, findings, oven_line=None):
    out = [f"# Scaled recipe: {path}", "", f"Scale: {how} -> factor x{factor:.3f}   Units: {target}", ""]
    out += ["| Ingredient | Original | Scaled | Also |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for it in items:
        out.append(f"| {it['ingredient']} | {it['original']} | {it['display']} | {it.get('also', '')} |")
    if oven_line:
        out += ["", f"Oven: {oven_line}"]
    out += ["", "## Notes", ""]
    if findings:
        out += ["| Severity | Code | Ingredient | Problem | Advice |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for f in findings:
            out.append(f"| {f['severity']} | {f['code']} | {f['ingredient']} | {f['problem']} | {f['fix']} |")
    else:
        out.append("No caveats.")
    out += ["", "Weights for volume ingredients use spoon-and-level densities; weigh flour if you can."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    cases = []
    def t(name, cond):
        cases.append((name, bool(cond)))
    close = lambda a, b, tol=1e-6: abs(a - b) <= tol
    t("parse 1 1/2", close(parse_qty("1 1/2"), 1.5))
    t("parse 3/4 and .5 and ½", close(parse_qty("3/4"), .75) and close(parse_qty(".5"), .5) and close(parse_qty("1½"), 1.5))
    t("bad quantity rejected", raises(lambda: parse_qty("some")))
    t("unit aliases", norm_unit("Tablespoons") == "tbsp" and norm_unit("T") == "tbsp" and norm_unit("t") == "tsp" and norm_unit("") == "each")
    t("unknown unit rejected", raises(lambda: norm_unit("handful")))
    t("longest density match", density_for("light brown sugar")[0] == "brown sugar" and density_for("all-purpose flour")[1] == 125)
    t("salt vs kosher salt", density_for("salt")[1] == 288 and density_for("kosher salt")[1] is None)
    t("eggs detected", egg_kind("large eggs") == "egg" and egg_kind("egg yolks") == "yolk" and egg_kind("eggplant") is None)
    a8 = parse_pan("8x8")[0]; a913 = parse_pan("9x13")[0]
    t("rect pan area", close(a8, 64) and close(a913, 117))
    t("round pan area", close(parse_pan("round9")[0], math.pi * 20.25))
    t("cm pan", close(parse_pan("20x20cm")[0], (20 / 2.54) ** 2))
    t("bad pan rejected", raises(lambda: parse_pan("big")))
    t("us volume 1 cup", fmt_us_volume(236.588) == "1 cup")
    t("us volume 3/4 cup", fmt_us_volume(ML["cup"] * .75) == "3/4 cup")
    t("us volume 2/3 cup", fmt_us_volume(ML["cup"] * 2 / 3) == "2/3 cup")
    t("us volume cup + tbsp", fmt_us_volume(ML["cup"] * 1.125) == "1 cup + 2 tbsp")
    t("fractions reduced, cups plural", fmt_us_volume(ML["cup"] * 0.61) == "1/2 cup + 2 tbsp" and fmt_us_volume(ML["cup"] * 2) == "2 cups")
    t("us volume tbsp", fmt_us_volume(ML["tbsp"] * 1.5) == "1 1/2 tbsp")
    t("us volume tsp", fmt_us_volume(ML["tsp"] * .5) == "1/2 tsp")
    t("us volume pinch", fmt_us_volume(ML["tsp"] * .05) == "pinch")
    t("metric rounding", round_metric(7.3) == 7.5 and round_metric(57.4) == 57 and round_metric(228) == 230 and round_metric(1234) == 1230)
    t("1 cup flour = 125 g", convert({"qty": 1, "unit": "cup", "ingredient": "all-purpose flour", "original": ""}, 1, "weight")["display"] == "125 g")
    t("1 stick butter in us/keep", "1 stick" in convert({"qty": 1, "unit": "stick", "ingredient": "butter", "original": ""}, 1, "keep")["display"])
    t("8 oz to grams", convert({"qty": 8, "unit": "oz", "ingredient": "cheese", "original": ""}, 1, "metric")["display"] == "225 g")
    t("500 g to us lb", convert({"qty": 500, "unit": "g", "ingredient": "pasta", "original": ""}, 1, "us")["display"] == "1 lb")
    t("metric volume", convert({"qty": 1, "unit": "cup", "ingredient": "milk", "original": ""}, 2, "metric")["display"] == "475 ml")
    t("no density keeps ml", "NO_DENSITY" in convert({"qty": 1, "unit": "tbsp", "ingredient": "fish sauce", "original": ""}, 1, "weight")["notes"])
    rows = read_recipe("quantity,unit,ingredient,note\n2,each,large eggs,\n1/4,tsp,baking soda,\n1,cup,sugar,\n")
    t("csv read", len(rows) == 3 and rows[0]["unit"] == "each")
    t("csv bad header rejected", raises(lambda: read_recipe("a,b\n1,2\n")))
    t("csv bad unit names line", "line 2" in err_of(lambda: read_recipe("quantity,unit,ingredient\n1,handful,x\n")))
    _, f = scale(rows, 1.828, baking=True)
    t("EGG_FRACTION at x1.83", any(x["code"] == "EGG_FRACTION" and "3 whole eggs plus 33 g" in x["fix"] for x in f))
    _, f = scale(rows, 2.0, baking=True)
    t("no EGG_FRACTION when whole", not any(x["code"] == "EGG_FRACTION" for x in f))
    _, f = scale(rows, 0.1, baking=True)
    t("TINY_AMOUNT and BIG_FACTOR", {"TINY_AMOUNT", "BIG_FACTOR", "LEAVENING"} <= {x["code"] for x in f})
    _, f = scale(rows, 1.0, baking=True, depth_ratio=1.83)
    t("DEPTH_CHANGE HIGH", any(x["code"] == "DEPTH_CHANGE" and x["severity"] == "HIGH" for x in f))
    _, f = scale(rows, 1.0, baking=True, depth_ratio=1.3)
    t("DEPTH_CHANGE MEDIUM", any(x["code"] == "DEPTH_CHANGE" and x["severity"] == "MEDIUM" for x in f))
    _, f = scale(read_recipe("quantity,unit,ingredient\n1,tsp,salt\n"), 3, baking=False)
    t("SEASONING and COOK_TIME for cooking", {"SEASONING", "COOK_TIME"} <= {x["code"] for x in f})
    t("oven F to C", oven("350F") == "350°F = 180°C (fan oven 160°C)" and oven("200C") == "200°C = 400°F")
    t("findings sorted HIGH first", scale(rows, 1.83, baking=True, depth_ratio=2)[1][0]["severity"] == "HIGH")
    passed = sum(ok for _, ok in cases)
    for name, ok in cases:
        print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + name)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(cases)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(cases) else 1


def raises(fn):
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return False


def err_of(fn):
    try:
        fn()
    except ValueError as e:
        return str(e)
    return ""


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("recipe", nargs="?")
    g = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    g.add_argument("--servings", nargs=2, type=float, metavar=("FROM", "TO"))
    g.add_argument("--factor", type=float)
    ap.add_argument("--from-pan")
    ap.add_argument("--to-pan")
    ap.add_argument("--to", default="keep", choices=["keep", "us", "metric", "weight"])
    ap.add_argument("--baking", action="store_true", help="apply baking caveats (eggs, leavening, pan depth)")
    ap.add_argument("--oven", help="original oven temperature, e.g. 350F or 180C")
    ap.add_argument("--time", help="original bake time in minutes, e.g. 20-25")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.recipe:
        ap.print_usage(sys.stderr); return 2
    try:
        rows = read_recipe(open(a.recipe, encoding="utf-8").read())
        depth_ratio = pan_change = None
        if bool(a.from_pan) != bool(a.to_pan):
            raise ValueError("give both --from-pan and --to-pan")
        if a.from_pan:
            fa, fd = parse_pan(a.from_pan)
            ta, td = parse_pan(a.to_pan)
            pan_change = f"{fd} -> {td}, area x{ta / fa:.2f}"
        if a.servings:
            if a.servings[0] <= 0 or a.servings[1] <= 0:
                raise ValueError("servings must be positive")
            factor, how = a.servings[1] / a.servings[0], f"{a.servings[0]:g} -> {a.servings[1]:g} servings"
        elif a.factor is not None:
            if a.factor <= 0:
                raise ValueError("factor must be positive")
            factor, how = a.factor, f"factor {a.factor:g}"
        elif a.from_pan:

# Reading Terraform plan output

## Get a machine-readable plan
```
terraform plan -out plan.out            # add -var-file / -target exactly as the real apply will
terraform show -json plan.out > plan.json
terraform show -no-color plan.out > plan.txt   # human-readable copy of the same saved plan
```
Review the SAME saved plan you will apply (`terraform apply plan.out`), not a fresh plan: state or remote resources can change in between. OpenTofu uses the same commands (`tofu show -json`) and format.

## Text symbols
| Symbol | Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `+` | `will be created` | new resource |
| `~` | `will be updated in-place` | attributes change, same resource ID |
| `-` | `will be destroyed` | resource deleted |
| `-/+` | `must be replaced` | destroy first, then create (default) - downtime gap |
| `+/-` | `must be replaced` | create first, then destroy (`create_before_destroy`) |
| `<=` | `will be read during apply` | data source read; check why it is unknown at plan time |
| `# forces replacement` | after an attribute | this attribute change causes the replacement |
| `(known after apply)` | value | computed; you cannot review it now |
| `(sensitive value)` | value | hidden in text output, but present in plan JSON |

Reason lines under a header: `# (because aws_x.y is not in configuration)` (removed from code or moved without a `moved` block), `# (because index [1] is out of range for count)` (count shrank or shifted), `# (because key ["a"] is not in for_each map)`, `# (resource is tainted, so must be replaced)`, `# (replace requested)` (`-replace=` flag).

Summary line: `Plan: 3 to add, 1 to change, 3 to destroy.` A replacement counts once in "add" and once in "destroy", so compare destroy count with the number of `-` and `-/+` headers.

## JSON structure (format_version 1.x)
```
{
  "format_version": "1.2", "terraform_version": "1.9.8",
  "resource_changes": [ {
      "address": "module.db.aws_db_instance.main", "module_address": "module.db",
      "mode": "managed" | "data", "type": "aws_db_instance", "name": "main", "index": 0 | "key",
      "change": {
        "actions": ["create"] | ["update"] | ["delete"] | ["delete","create"] | ["create","delete"] | ["no-op"] | ["read"] | ["forget"],
        "before": {...} | null, "after": {...} | null,
        "after_unknown": {"id": true},              # values known only after apply
        "before_sensitive": {...}, "after_sensitive": {"password": true},
        "replace_paths": [["storage_encrypted"]],   # attributes that force replacement
        "importing": {"id": "..."}                  # import blocks (1.5+)
      },
      "action_reason": "replace_because_cannot_update" | "replace_because_tainted" | "replace_by_request" |
                       "delete_because_no_resource_config" | "delete_because_count_index" | "delete_because_each_key" | ...,
      "previous_address": "aws_db_instance.old"     # moved blocks
  } ],
  "resource_drift": [ ... changes made outside Terraform ... ],
  "output_changes": {...}, "prior_state": {...}, "configuration": {...},
  "applyable": true, "complete": true, "errored": false
}
```
Useful one-liners:
```
jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions != ["no-op"]) | "\(.change.actions | join(",")) \(.address)"' plan.json
jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("delete")) | .address' plan.json
jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.replace_paths) | "\(.address): \(.change.replace_paths)"' plan.json
```

## Secrets in plans
`before`/`after` contain real values, including passwords and private keys, even when `*_sensitive` marks them. Treat plan.out and plan.json like secrets: do not attach them to tickets, chats or public CI logs; keep them as short-lived, access-controlled CI artifacts. Share the risk summary instead.

## What a plan cannot tell you
- Values computed at apply time (`known after apply`), including many IAM policy documents built from other resources.
- Side effects outside Terraform: DNS caches, clients pinned to an IP, data inside a database being replaced.
- Whether `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` is set (it is in `configuration`, and a plan that would violate it fails instead).
- Provider-specific behaviour such as RDS applying some changes only in the next maintenance window (`apply_immediately`).

# Risk rules used by plan_risk.py

| Code | Severity | Trigger | Why it matters | Typical fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DATA_LOSS | HIGH | destroy or replace of a data-holding type: databases (RDS, Cloud SQL, Azure SQL/PostgreSQL/MySQL, Cosmos DB, DynamoDB), buckets, disks/volumes, EFS/FSx, caches, queues/streams, KMS keys, secrets, DNS zones, log groups, ECR, Kubernetes PVCs/namespaces | a new resource starts empty; KMS key deletion makes encrypted data unreadable | snapshot/backup first, `moved` block for refactors, `prevent_destroy` on data stores, migrate data before replacing |
| PROTECTION_OFF | HIGH (update) / MEDIUM (new or replaced) | `deletion_protection`, `deletion_protection_enabled`, `enable_deletion_protection`, `termination_protection`, `disable_api_termination` false | the next mistake can delete production | keep true; disable only in a separate change right before a planned delete |
| PUBLIC_INGRESS | HIGH | new 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress on all ports or admin/data ports (22, 3389, 3306, 5432, 1433, 6379, 27017, 9200, 6443 ...) | direct attack surface, brute force, data exposure | known CIDRs, SSM Session Manager, VPN, bastion, private endpoints |
| PUBLIC_INGRESS | MEDIUM / INFO | other ports / 80 and 443 | | expose only load balancers |
| PUBLIC_DATABASE | HIGH | `publicly_accessible = true` | database endpoint reachable from the internet | private subnets, proxy, VPN |
| S3_PUBLIC_ACCESS | HIGH | any of the four public access block settings set to false | bucket policies or ACLs can make data public | keep all four true; CloudFront + Origin Access Control |
| PUBLIC_ACL | HIGH | `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `authenticated-read` | everyone can list or read (or write) | BucketOwnerEnforced, private |
| PUBLIC_POLICY | HIGH | resource policy Allow with Principal `*` and no Condition | anyone on the internet (or any AWS account) gets access | named principals; `aws:SourceArn`, `aws:PrincipalOrgID`, `aws:SourceVpce` |
| PUBLIC_IAM | HIGH | GCP binding to `allUsers` / `allAuthenticatedUsers` | public access | specific members |
| TRUST_ANYONE | HIGH | role trust policy with Principal `*` and no Condition | any AWS account can assume the role | exact ARNs + `sts:ExternalId` |
| IAM_ADMIN | HIGH | `Action * / Resource *`, AdministratorAccess, PowerUserAccess, IAMFullAccess, GCP owner/editor, Azure Owner/User Access Administrator (Contributor = MEDIUM) | full control of the account or project | least privilege; break-glass admin with MFA |
| IAM_ESCALATION | HIGH | `iam:PassRole`, `iam:Attach*/Put*Policy`, `iam:CreatePolicyVersion`, `iam:CreateAccessKey`, `sts:AssumeRole`, `kms:*` on `*`; `iam:*`, `sts:*` anywhere | the holder can grant itself more rights | scope to specific ARNs; `iam:PassedToService` condition |
| IAM_WILDCARD | HIGH on `*` / MEDIUM | `service:*` actions, `*FullAccess` managed policies | far more than needed, includes delete | list actions actually used (Access Analyzer, CloudTrail) |
| IAM_NOT_ACTION | MEDIUM | Allow with NotAction | grants everything else, including future actions | explicit Action list |
| IAM_WIDENED | LOW | update adds actions or resources to a policy | permission creep | confirm with the owner |
| TRUST_WIDENED | MEDIUM | new principals in a trust policy | new cross-account access | confirm each principal |
| NO_FINAL_SNAPSHOT | MEDIUM | `skip_final_snapshot = true` on RDS/Aurora/DocumentDB/Neptune/Redshift | deleting leaves nothing to restore | `false` + `final_snapshot_identifier` |
| FORCE_DESTROY | MEDIUM | `force_destroy = true` newly set | delete wipes all objects or records | keep false on real data |
| ENCRYPTION_OFF | MEDIUM | `storage_encrypted`/`encrypted` false | compliance; enabling later usually forces replacement | enable now |
| BACKUPS_OFF | MEDIUM | `backup_retention_period = 0` | no point-in-time recovery | 7 to 35 days |
| SECRET_REGENERATED | MEDIUM | replace of `random_password`, `random_string`, `tls_private_key`, `aws_iam_access_key` | consumers break | plan the rotation |
| COUNT_INDEX_SHIFT | MEDIUM | `delete_because_count_index` | removing a middle item destroys and recreates the following ones | `for_each` with stable keys, `moved` blocks |
| DESTROY | MEDIUM (compute, LB, IP, cluster, count/each removal) / LOW | non-stateful destroy | downtime, lost IPs | confirm intent; `moved` for refactors |
| REPLACE | MEDIUM (destroy-first compute/LB) / LOW | non-stateful replace | new IDs, IPs, DNS names; downtime gap | `create_before_destroy`, check dependents |
| PUBLIC_FUNCTION_URL | MEDIUM | Lambda URL with auth NONE | public endpoint | AWS_IAM auth |
| PLAN_ERRORED / PLAN_INCOMPLETE | HIGH / MEDIUM | `errored` / `complete: false` | partial picture | re-plan |
| DRIFT, REMOVED_FROM_CONFIG, MOVED, IMPORT, FORGET, POLICY_UNKNOWN, TEXT_MODE | INFO | context | | |

## Verdict
- Any HIGH: do not apply until each HIGH is fixed or explicitly accepted by the owner (name and reason in the review).
- Only MEDIUM: apply after the owner of each affected resource agrees.
- LOW/INFO only: normal review.

## Things to check by hand
- **Blast radius:** how many resources change, and are they all expected from the code diff? A one-line change that replaces 40 resources is a red flag (provider upgrade, changed `name`, `count` to `for_each`).
- **Order and downtime:** destroy-first replacements of anything serving traffic; DNS TTLs; target group swaps.
- **Data migration:** a replaced database needs a restore from snapshot or a data migration plan; Terraform will not copy data.
- **Unknown values:** policies or security group rules that are `known after apply` - review the module code instead.
- **Provider and module upgrades:** read the changelog for forced replacements and default changes.
- **Environment:** confirm the workspace/backend (`terraform workspace show`) and account (`aws sts get-caller-identity`) before applying.
- **Policy as code:** OPA/Conftest, Sentinel, Checkov or tfsec rules can enforce the HIGH checks in CI.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Terraform plan risk reviewer (Python 3 standard library only).

Reads `terraform show -json plan.out` output (or, with less detail, the text of
`terraform plan -no-color`) and flags risky changes: destroys and replacements of
stateful resources (data loss), removed deletion protection, skipped final
snapshots, force_destroy, disabled encryption, new public network exposure
(0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress, public databases, S3 public access blocks, public ACLs
and policies, allUsers bindings), IAM widening (wildcard actions, admin policies,
iam:PassRole on *, trust policies open to anyone) and count index shifts. Prints a
risk summary. Never prints attribute values that Terraform marks as sensitive.

Usage:
  terraform plan -out plan.out && terraform show -json plan.out > plan.json
  python3 plan_risk.py plan.json [--json]
  terraform plan -no-color > plan.txt && python3 plan_risk.py plan.txt   (text mode)
  python3 plan_risk.py --self-test
Exit codes: 0 = no HIGH findings, 1 = HIGH findings, 2 = unreadable input.
"""
import argparse, json, re, sys

SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2, "INFO": 3}
STATEFUL = re.compile(r"^(aws_(db_instance|rds_cluster|dynamodb_table|s3_bucket|ebs_volume|efs_file_system|"
                      r"elasticache_(cluster|replication_group)|redshift_cluster|docdb_cluster|neptune_cluster|"
                      r"opensearch_domain|elasticsearch_domain|kinesis_stream|sqs_queue|kms_key|secretsmanager_secret|"
                      r"backup_vault|ecr_repository|cloudwatch_log_group|msk_cluster|fsx_\w+|route53_zone|"
                      r"cognito_user_pool|timestream_table)|"
                      r"google_(sql_database_instance|sql_database|storage_bucket|bigquery_(dataset|table)|compute_disk|"
                      r"spanner_(instance|database)|kms_crypto_key|redis_instance|filestore_instance|firestore_database|"
                      r"dns_managed_zone)|"
                      r"azurerm_(storage_account|storage_container|mssql_(database|server)|postgresql_flexible_server|"
                      r"mysql_flexible_server|cosmosdb_account|key_vault|managed_disk|redis_cache|dns_zone)|"
                      r"kubernetes_(persistent_volume_claim|persistent_volume|namespace)(_v1)?)$")
SECRET_GEN = re.compile(r"^(random_password|random_string|tls_private_key|aws_iam_access_key)$")
DOWNTIME = re.compile(r"^(aws_(instance|lb|alb|eip|nat_gateway|cloudfront_distribution|api_gateway_rest_api|"
                      r"eks_cluster|ecs_service|acm_certificate)|google_(compute_instance|container_cluster)|"
                      r"azurerm_(linux|windows)_virtual_machine|azurerm_kubernetes_cluster)$")
SENSITIVE_PORTS = {22: "SSH", 23: "Telnet", 3389: "RDP", 3306: "MySQL", 5432: "PostgreSQL", 1433: "SQL Server",
                   1521: "Oracle", 6379: "Redis", 27017: "MongoDB", 9200: "Elasticsearch", 5601: "Kibana",
                   2375: "Docker API", 2379: "etcd", 11211: "Memcached", 5900: "VNC", 9092: "Kafka",
                   6443: "Kubernetes API", 10250: "Kubelet"}
WEB_PORTS = {80, 443}
PUBLIC_CIDRS = {"0.0.0.0/0", "::/0", "*", "internet", "any"}
ADMIN_POLICIES = re.compile(r"(AdministratorAccess|PowerUserAccess|IAMFullAccess)$")
ESCALATION_ACTIONS = {"iam:*", "iam:passrole", "iam:createpolicyversion", "iam:attachrolepolicy", "iam:putrolepolicy",
                      "iam:createaccesskey", "iam:updateassumerolepolicy", "sts:assumerole", "sts:*", "kms:*", "*"}
POLICY_ATTRS = ("policy", "assume_role_policy", "inline_policy")
PROTECTION_ATTRS = ("deletion_protection", "deletion_protection_enabled", "enable_deletion_protection",
                    "termination_protection", "disable_api_termination")


def finding(sev, code, addr, problem, fix):
    return {"severity": sev, "code": code, "resource": addr, "problem": problem, "fix": fix}


def kind_of(actions):
    a = list(actions or [])
    if a == ["delete", "create"]:
        return "replace (destroy first)"
    if a == ["create", "delete"]:
        return "replace (create first)"
    return {"create": "create", "update": "update", "delete": "destroy", "no-op": "no-op", "read": "read",
            "forget": "forget"}.get(a[0] if len(a) == 1 else ",".join(a), ",".join(a))


def sensitive(mask, key):
    return mask is True or (isinstance(mask, dict) and mask.get(key) not in (None, False))


def get(d, key, default=None):
    return d.get(key, default) if isinstance(d, dict) else default


def ports_of(lo, hi, proto):
    proto = str(proto).lower()
    if proto in ("-1", "all", "*"):
        return 0, 65535, "all"
    try:
        lo, hi = int(lo if lo not in (None, "") else 0), int(hi if hi not in (None, "") else 65535)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0, 65535, proto
    if proto in ("icmp", "icmpv6", "1", "58"):
        return None
    if lo in (-1,) or (lo == 0 and hi in (0, 65535)):
        return 0, 65535, proto
    return lo, hi, proto


def open_rules(rtype, values):
    """Yield (cidr, lo, hi, proto) for internet-open ingress rules in a resource's values."""
    v = values or {}
    out = set()
    def add(cidrs, lo, hi, proto):
        p = ports_of(lo, hi, proto)
        if p is None:
            return
        for c in cidrs or []:
            if str(c).lower() in PUBLIC_CIDRS:
                out.add((str(c), p[0], p[1], p[2]))
    if rtype == "aws_security_group":
        for r in v.get("ingress") or []:
            add((r.get("cidr_blocks") or []) + (r.get("ipv6_cidr_blocks") or []), r.get("from_port"), r.get("to_port"), r.get("protocol"))
    elif rtype == "aws_security_group_rule" and v.get("type") == "ingress":
        add((v.get("cidr_blocks") or []) + (v.get("ipv6_cidr_blocks") or []), v.get("from_port"), v.get("to_port"), v.get("protocol"))
    elif rtype == "aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule":
        add([x for x in (v.get("cidr_ipv4"), v.get("cidr_ipv6")) if x], v.get("from_port"), v.get("to_port"), v.get("ip_protocol"))
    elif rtype == "google_compute_firewall" and str(v.get("direction", "INGRESS")).upper() == "INGRESS":
        for al in v.get("allow") or []:
            ports = al.get("ports") or ["0-65535"]
            for pr in ports:
                lo, _, hi = str(pr).partition("-")
                add(v.get("source_ranges"), lo, hi or lo, al.get("protocol", "all"))
    elif rtype == "azurerm_network_security_rule" and str(v.get("direction")).lower() == "inbound" and str(v.get("access")).lower() == "allow":
        src = [v.get("source_address_prefix")] + (v.get("source_address_prefixes") or [])
        rng = v.get("destination_port_range") or "*"
        for pr in [rng] + (v.get("destination_port_ranges") or []):
            if pr == "*":
                add(src, 0, 65535, v.get("protocol", "*"))
            else:
                lo, _, hi = str(pr).partition("-")
                add(src, lo, hi or lo, v.get("protocol", "*"))
    return out


def port_label(lo, hi, proto):
    if proto == "all" or (lo == 0 and hi == 65535):
        return "all ports"
    names = [f"{p} ({n})" for p, n in SENSITIVE_PORTS.items() if lo <= p <= hi]
    rng = str(lo) if lo == hi else f"{lo}-{hi}"
    return f"port {rng}" + (f" incl. {', '.join(names[:3])}" if names and lo != hi else (f" ({SENSITIVE_PORTS[lo]})" if lo == hi and lo in SENSITIVE_PORTS else ""))


def parse_policy(doc):
    if isinstance(doc, str):
        try:
            doc = json.loads(doc)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
        return None
    st = doc.get("Statement") or []
    return [st] if isinstance(st, dict) else st


def as_list(x):
    return x if isinstance(x, list) else ([] if x is None else [x])


def allow_actions(stmts):
    acts = set()
    for s in stmts or []:
        if s.get("Effect", "Allow") != "Allow":
            continue
        for a in as_list(s.get("Action")):
            for r in as_list(s.get("Resource")) or ["(none)"]:
                acts.add((str(a), str(r)))
    return acts


def check_policy(addr, attr, before, after, unknown):
    out = []
    if unknown:
        return [finding("INFO", "POLICY_UNKNOWN", addr, f"{attr} is only known after apply", "Review the rendered policy after apply or render it with a data source in a separate plan.")]
    b, a = parse_policy(before), parse_policy(after)
    if a is None:
        return out
    if attr == "assume_role_policy":
        for s in a:
            if s.get("Effect", "Allow") != "Allow":
                continue
            pr = s.get("Principal")
            vals = [pr] if isinstance(pr, str) else [v for x in (pr or {}).values() for v in as_list(x)]
            if "*" in vals and not s.get("Condition"):
                out.append(finding("HIGH", "TRUST_ANYONE", addr, "trust policy lets any AWS principal assume this role (Principal * without Condition)",
                                   "Name the exact account or role ARNs, and add sts:ExternalId or aws:PrincipalOrgID conditions."))
        bp = {v for s in (b or []) for x in (get(s, "Principal") or {}).values() for v in as_list(x)} if b and all(isinstance(get(s, "Principal"), dict) for s in b) else set()
        ap = {v for s in a if isinstance(s.get("Principal"), dict) for x in s["Principal"].values() for v in as_list(x)}
        new = sorted(ap - bp - {"*"})
        if b is not None and new:
            out.append(finding("MEDIUM", "TRUST_WIDENED", addr, "new principals can assume this role: " + ", ".join(new), "Confirm each new principal is expected (cross-account access?)."))
        return out
    for s in a:
        if s.get("Effect", "Allow") != "Allow":
            continue
        orig = [str(x) for x in as_list(s.get("Action"))]
        acts = [x.lower() for x in orig]
        res = [str(x) for x in as_list(s.get("Resource"))]
        pr = s.get("Principal")
        if pr is not None:
            vals = [pr] if isinstance(pr, str) else [v for x in pr.values() for v in as_list(x)]
            if "*" in vals and not s.get("Condition"):
                out.append(finding("HIGH", "PUBLIC_POLICY", addr, f"resource policy allows Principal * ({', '.join(acts)[:80]}) without a Condition",
                                   "Restrict Principal to known ARNs or add aws:SourceArn / aws:PrincipalOrgID / aws:SourceVpce conditions; use CloudFront OAC for public sites."))
        if s.get("NotAction"):
            out.append(finding("MEDIUM", "IAM_NOT_ACTION", addr, "Allow with NotAction grants everything except the listed actions", "List the allowed actions explicitly."))
        if "*" in acts and "*" in res:
            out.append(finding("HIGH", "IAM_ADMIN", addr, "Allow Action * on Resource * (full admin)", "Grant only the actions and resources this principal needs."))
            continue
        esc = sorted({o for o, x in zip(orig, acts) if x in ESCALATION_ACTIONS and x != "*" and ("*" in res or x in ("iam:*", "sts:*"))})
        if esc:
            out.append(finding("HIGH", "IAM_ESCALATION", addr, f"{', '.join(esc)} on {', '.join(res) or '*'} lets the holder gain more privileges",
                               "Scope iam:PassRole and sts:AssumeRole to specific role ARNs (and iam:PassedToService); avoid iam:* and kms:* wildcards."))
        wild = sorted({o for o, x in zip(orig, acts) if x.endswith(":*") and x not in ESCALATION_ACTIONS})
        if wild:
            sev = "HIGH" if "*" in res else "MEDIUM"
            out.append(finding(sev, "IAM_WILDCARD", addr, f"service wildcard {', '.join(wild)} on {', '.join(res)}",
                               "Replace with the specific actions used (check IAM Access Analyzer or CloudTrail for what is actually called)."))
    if b is not None:
        added = sorted({x[0] + (" on " + x[1] if x[1] not in ("*", "(none)") else " on *") for x in allow_actions(a) - allow_actions(b)})
        if added:
            out.append(finding("LOW", "IAM_WIDENED", addr, "policy grants new actions/resources: " + ", ".join(added[:8]) + (" ..." if len(added) > 8 else ""),
                               "Confirm the new permissions are needed; least privilege."))
    return out


def review_change(rc):
    out = []
    addr, rtype = rc.get("address", "?"), rc.get("type", "")
    ch = rc.get("change") or {}
    actions = ch.get("actions") or []

    before, after = ch.get("before") or {}, ch.get("after") or {}
    unknown = ch.get("after_unknown") or {}
    reason = rc.get("action_reason", "")
    if rc.get("mode") == "data" or kind in ("no-op", "read"):
        return kind, out
    why = ""

        if get(after, "skip_final_snapshot") is True and rtype in ("aws_db_instance", "aws_rds_cluster", "aws_docdb_cluster", "aws_neptune_cluster", "aws_redshift_cluster"):
            if kind != "update" or get(before, "skip_final_snapshot") is not True:
                out.append(finding("MEDIUM", "NO_FINAL_SNAPSHOT", addr, "skip_final_snapshot = true: a delete leaves no snapshot",
                                   "Set skip_final_snapshot = false with a final_snapshot_identifier."))
        if get(after, "force_destroy") is True and (kind != "update" or get(before, "force_destroy") is not True):

            if get(after, attr) is False and (kind != "update" or get(before, attr) is True):

        if get(after, "backup_retention_period") == 0 and get(before, "backup_retention_period", 1) != 0:
            out.append(finding("MEDIUM", "BACKUPS_OFF", addr, "backup_retention_period = 0 disables automated backups", "Keep at least 7 days for production databases."))
        if get(after, "publicly_accessible") is True and get(before, "publicly_accessible") is not True:
            out.append(finding("HIGH", "PUBLIC_DATABASE", addr, "publicly_accessible = true gives the database a public endpoint",
                               "Keep databases private; connect through a bastion, VPN, SSM or RDS Proxy."))
        if rtype == "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block":

            if off:

        if rtype in ("aws_s3_bucket_acl", "aws_s3_object") and get(after, "acl") in ("public-read", "public-read-write", "authenticated-read"):
            out.append(finding("HIGH", "PUBLIC_ACL", addr, f"acl = {after['acl']}", "Use private ACLs (BucketOwnerEnforced) and CloudFront for public files."))
